overridesNotes.tar: The root tree resolves tar@7.5.11 through lerna (directly, and again under its pacote / @npmcli/arborist / node-gyp subtrees), which is still inside the same series of node-tar advisories already pinned in packages/app — up to the critical file-smuggling one patched in 7.5.21. Scope here is dev-only release tooling; nothing from the root manifest ships. The floor matches packages/app so both trees resolve to the same tar and a fresh install cannot drift back into an advisory range.
overridesNotes.js-yaml: js-yaml@4.1.1 arrives via eslint@8, lerna (which pins the exact version 4.1.1) and @intlify/vue-i18n-loader. The advisories against it are fixed in 4.3.1, and GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh (maxTotalMergeKeys does not bound CPU use for empty merge sources) moves the floor to 4.3.2. This stays inside the v4 major, where the load/dump API is unchanged (v4 had already dropped the safeLoad/safeDump aliases), so every consumer keeps working. packages/app pins 4.3.2 as a direct dependency for the same reason.
overridesNotes.pacote: lerna@9.0.7 pins pacote to the exact version 21.0.1, and its @npmcli/arborist subtree resolves a second copy at 21.5.0; both sit inside GHSA-w4pp-8pjf-rmxw (DoS via addGitSha, patched in 21.5.1). Because lerna's pin is exact, a plain lockfile refresh cannot move it, and lerna 9.0.7 is the latest release, so the override is the only way to reach the patched version. 21.5.1 is a patch inside the same major that lerna already targets; pacote@22 is deliberately not used. Dev-scope only: lerna is release tooling and nothing from the root manifest ships.
overridesNotes.smol-toml: nx pins smol-toml@1.6.1. Keep the override within v1 and require >=1.9.1 to cover GHSA-7w5x-hrqm-74c2 and GHSA-r4xh-jqrq-34v2. Used only by release tooling.
overridesNotes.nx/brace-expansion: nx pins brace-expansion@5.0.8. Require >=5.0.12 for GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895, GHSA-6j4f-fj2g-mc7p, GHSA-qhr7-859c-m2p7 and GHSA-q2hr-2g5m-vwhr. Scope to nx; explicitly retain brace-expansion@1.x under minimatch@3 so npm cannot reuse an incompatible named-export module for its function call.
